thread:
kevin.chen: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night's prod OOMs — recurring mem surges on prod-rt-cache. Root suspects: KV fragmentation + slow background GC on high-shard pods. Listing action items and owners below.

priya.desai: Can you drop the profiling links? want to see heap/alloc flamegraphs.

kevin.chen: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/rt-cache/mem-growth (look at 03:10–03:40)
flamegraphs: s3://redwood-artifacts/rt-cache/2026-03-21/flame-03-15.svg

nate: saw repeated small allocs and many short-lived kv entries — suspect slab fragmentation. i'm for enabling slab compaction profile and running a 24h heap-scan.

jess: i'm happy to own the canary rollout of softlimits + eviction tuning (small batch). will create canary config and watch latency.

maria: recommend adding a rate-of-growth alert: rule proposal -> `heap_growth_rate_1h > 10%` + `kv_eviction_ratio < 0.8` for 15m. avoids noisy single-spike alerts.

kevin.chen: Action items (short):
- A1 (owner: priya.desai) — run continuous heap profiling for 48h, produce flamegraphs + top alloc stacks. due: 2026-03-28
- A2 (owner: nate) — enable slab compaction flag + run offline workload to measure fragmentation delta. due: 2026-03-25
- A3 (owner: jess) — create canary config with softlimit=0.85 and eviction-policy=age-based; 6h canary then rollback. due: 2026-03-24
- A4 (owner: kevin.chen) — add two alerts to prod: heap_growth_rate_1h and kv_eviction_ratio; validate noise. due: 2026-03-22
- A5 (owner: maria) — synth test that creates many short-lived kv keys to reproduce allocation pattern; attach workload to PR. due: 2026-03-26

priya.desai: started profiler job: `./tools/heap-prof --target prod-rt-cache --duration 48h --out s3://redwood-artifacts/rt-cache/2026-03-21/`
will post interim results by EOD.

nate: experiment notes: enabling `--slab-compact=1` reduced fragmentation index from 0.42 -> 0.29 on local harness. pushing a benchmark run now and will open an infra PR with the flag guarded by feature-flag.

jess: created canary config and PR: https://git.redwood/infraprod/PR-4578 — scheduling canary for 03/23 10:00 UTC, will monitor token latency and allocation trends.

incident-bot: Runbook draft created: https://docs.redwood/internal/rt-cache/runbooks/memory-recurrence — draft PR #2345 opened by kevin.chen

maria: adding a recurring weekly retro item to track recurrence patterns and check cumulative mem growth across releases. propose cadence: weekly until no regressions for 4 consecutive weeks.

kevin.chen: owners — please update the action item checklist in the runbook PR, ping me when your PRs are ready. We'll meet 03/24 15:00 UTC for a 30m sync (owners only).

jess: noted. I'll include a synthetic load step in the canary playbook so we don't miss the short-lived kv pattern.

priya.desai: interim findings: top allocs show heavy bytes from `kv::insert` path where tombstones linger ~minutes; looks like GC sweep interval is tuned coarsely. I'll detail stack traces in the PR.

nate: question: do we want automatic fallback to a smaller model (lower mem) in severe cases? might be out of scope for runtime but good to discuss with product.

kevin.chen: make a short note in the runbook about fallback policy options; we'll take product follow-up separately. For now focus on profiling, slab compaction, canary, alerts, and synth tests.

maria: i'll add the weekly recurrence item in the retro board and invite SRE + runtime leads.

kevin.chen: thanks — last thing: please add estimated rollout windows and rollback steps to each PR. closing thread after sync on 03/24. :thumbsup:
